title: LeakFrame
summary: Inspect JPEGs for location and identity-adjacent metadata, then create a lossless cleaned copy locally without re-encoding the compressed image data.
problem: Photos can carry EXIF location, camera, timestamp, XMP, IPTC and comments that users may not realize they are sharing alongside the visible image.
audience: People who share photos or screenshots publicly and want a quick local privacy check before uploading.
why_now: Helpfeel confirmed in September 2026 that exposed Gyazo image metadata included EXIF location data when present, making hidden photo metadata a concrete current privacy concern rather than an abstract warning.
difference: LeakFrame combines a readable risk summary with a local cleaning step that keeps the original file and strips JPEG privacy metadata segments without re-encoding the compressed image stream.
monetization_hypothesis: Best kept as a free local privacy utility; a paid desktop batch workflow would require separate demand validation.
limitations: Only JPG/JPEG is supported in this version.
It detects the presence of GPS metadata but intentionally does not print precise coordinates.
It preserves APP2 ICC color profiles and may not understand vendor-specific metadata outside EXIF/XMP/IPTC/comment segments.

alternatives.name: ExifTool
alternatives.difference: ExifTool is a comprehensive metadata CLI supporting many formats and tag families; LeakFrame offers a much smaller share-before-you-post flow with plain-language privacy flags and a safe sibling output file.

alternatives.name: LocalTools Remove EXIF Data
alternatives.difference: LocalTools provides a browser-based multi-format cleaner; LeakFrame is a zero-dependency local script that reports what it found and removes JPEG metadata segments without re-encoding the compressed scan data.
